title: gustar: agree, disagree and say how much
intro: 10 tasks: listen and write, rewrite, find the mistake, match reactions and fill a table with encantar.

items.text: —No me gusta el invierno. —A mí tampoco.
items.explanation: Tampoco agrees with a negative sentence: a mí tampoco = me neither.

items.text: A Diego le gusta mucho jugar al fútbol con sus amigos.
items.explanation: An action you like is an infinitive after gusta; mucho comes after the verb. Jugar al fútbol: a + el = al.

items.source: A mi padre y a mi madre les gusta pasear.
items.explanation: Mis padres are two people → les. Pasear is an action (infinitive), so the verb stays gusta.

items.source: La música clásica no me gusta.
items.explanation: No goes before the pronoun, and the thing you like can come at the end: No me gusta la música clásica.
For ellos, ellas and ustedes the pronoun is les.

items.prompt:
—A mí me gusta mucho el verano.
—A mí ___. (Me too.)
items.explanation: To agree with a positive sentence, say a mí también.

items.prompt: A mi abuela le ___ las flores. (encantar)
items.explanation: Encantar works like gustar: las flores is plural, so the verb is encantan.
The person who likes something needs a: A Valentina le gusta mucho pintar.

items.prompt: Match each Spanish phrase with its English meaning.
pairs: I don't like it at all.
items.explanation: Encanta is stronger than gusta mucho; no … nada means “not at all”. También answers a positive sentence, tampoco a negative one.

items.prompt: Who loves animals? Write the pronoun and the verb.
items.explanation: Only the pronoun changes: me, te, le, nos, os, les. The verb stays encantan because los animales is plural.
